name: Beliefs
big_question: What do people believe, and how do they show those beliefs?

an idea that someone accepts as true or real

lessons.title: Why study RE?
lessons.big_question: What is the importance of RE? Why do we study it?
aims: DESCRIBE — what Religious Education is
DISCUSS — why RE matters in a world of many religions
EXPLAIN — how RE builds respect and empathy

questions: Write down three reasons why it is important to study RE.
Name any three religions you have heard of.
How should you behave in an RE lesson? Give two rules.

learn.caption: Why Religious Education matters
rows: 8 billion people live in the world

source.quote: The United Nations estimates that there are 8 billion people living in the world today. 85% of the people, or 7 billion people in the world, are religious.
source.attrib: — Unit 1 lesson slides, on why we study RE
source.task: Underline the two numbers in the quote. Then write one sentence on why RE is worth studying.

stretch.question: Explain two reasons why we study Religious Education.

debate.statement: Everyone should study Religious Education at school.
agree: Most of the world is religious, so RE helps you understand the people around you.
RE teaches respect and empathy, which you need when you travel or try new foods.
disagree: One billion people are not religious, so some students may feel RE is not for them.
School time is short, and some people think subjects like maths matter more.
debate.how_to_win: Use the numbers from the slides, then say which side has the stronger reason and why.

quickfire.q: What do the letters RE stand for?
What is the definition of Religious Education?
How many people live in the world today?
What percentage of people are religious?
How many people are not religious?
Name two virtues that RE promotes.

lessons.title: Baseline test
lessons.big_question: How much do I already know about religion and belief?
aims: DESCRIBE — key words about God, holy books and worship
DISCUSS — which answers I found easy and which were hard
EXPLAIN — two reasons why we study religious education

questions: What is Religious Education? Answer in a full sentence.
Give two reasons why studying RE is important.
What percentage of the world's people are religious?

learn.caption: Topics your baseline test covers
rows: Holy books and places of worship
Polytheism: the belief in many Gods
Two reasons why we study RE

source.quote: Theism is the belief there is God. Atheists are people who do not believe in God. Agnostics are people who are not sure God exists.
source.attrib: — Unit 1 baseline test, key word definitions
source.task: Copy the three key words into your book. Highlight the one word that means belief in God.

stretch.question: Outline two reasons why we study religious education.

debate.statement: A test at the start of a unit is a waste of lesson time.
agree: You cannot be tested on things you have not been taught yet, so the marks feel unfair.
The time could be spent learning new facts about religion instead of sitting in silence.
disagree: A baseline test shows your teacher what you already know, so lessons can be pitched right.
Comparing it with the end test proves how much you have learned in the unit.
debate.how_to_win: Say what a baseline test is for, then judge whether that purpose is worth one lesson.

lessons.title: What is a belief?
lessons.big_question: What is a belief and why do people hold different beliefs?
aims: DESCRIBE — what a belief, a fact and an opinion are
DISCUSS — which statements are facts and which are opinions
EXPLAIN — the difference between a belief and a fact

questions: List three facts about any religion that you already know.
Which baseline test question did you find hardest? Why?
What is the study of religion called?

learn.caption: Belief, fact and opinion
rows: Belief: accepted as true or real
Fact: it can be proven true

source.quote: A belief is an idea that someone accepts as true or real. A fact is a statement or idea that can be proven true. An opinion expresses how someone feels about something.
source.attrib: — Unit 1 lesson slides, on belief, fact and opinion
source.task: Sort these three into fact, opinion or belief: water boils at 100C; mint choc chip is best; murder is wrong.

stretch.question: Explain the difference between a fact and an opinion.

debate.statement: A belief is not worth as much as a fact.
agree: A fact can be proven true, but a belief cannot be proven, so facts are more reliable.
Science works on facts, and a fact stays the same no matter how anyone feels about it.
disagree: Beliefs guide how billions of people live, so they matter enormously in real life.
Important ideas, like the idea that murder is wrong, are beliefs and cannot be proven.
debate.how_to_win: Define fact and belief first, then say what each one is actually useful for.

quickfire.q: Define theism.
What is a place of worship?
Why is it important to study RE?
What is a holy book?
What is a belief?
What is an opinion?

lessons.title: Is seeing believing?
aims: DESCRIBE — what theists, atheists and agnostics believe
DISCUSS — whether everyone sees the world the same way
EXPLAIN — how Christians and Muslims show belief in God

questions: Have you ever seen something that was not real? Describe it.
Can you believe in something you cannot see? Give one example.
What is the difference between a fact and an opinion?

learn.caption: Ways of seeing and ways of showing belief
rows: Theism: belief that there is a God
Atheist: does not believe in God

source.quote: People who follow a religion may see the same world as everyone else but perceive it differently. In RE we look at those different ways of seeing the world and try to understand them.
source.attrib: — Unit 1 lesson slides, on is seeing believing
source.task: Look at an optical illusion with a partner. Write what you each saw, then why it differed.

stretch.question: Explain two ways that believers show their belief in God.

debate.statement: You should only believe in things you can see.
agree: If you cannot see something there is no proof it is there, so believing is only guessing.
Optical illusions show that even our own eyes can trick us, so we need real evidence.
disagree: Nobody can see kindness or love, but almost everyone agrees these things are real.
Millions of Muslims and Christians pray to a God they cannot see and it changes their lives.
debate.how_to_win: Use one optical illusion example and one prayer example, then say which side is stronger.

quickfire.q: What is a belief?
Give an example of a fact and an opinion.
What is a fact?
Define religious education.
Define agnostic.
What are the Friday prayers for Muslims called?

lessons.title: Is there a God?
lessons.big_question: Is there a God, and if so why do people disagree?
aims: DESCRIBE — what a theist, atheist and agnostic believe
DISCUSS — why people in Britain disagree about God
EXPLAIN — two different beliefs about God in Britain

questions: Do you believe in God? Give a convincing argument for or against.
Define atheist in a full sentence.
What happens in Muslim Friday prayer?

learn.caption: Three views people hold about God
rows: Atheist: does not believe in God
Agnostic: not sure if God exists

source.quote: Amir prays everyday because he believes God listens to him. Sophia says there is no evidence for God, so she does not believe God exists.
source.attrib: — Unit 1 lesson slides, on views about God
source.task: Luca says nobody can be certain if God exists. Which of the three views is Luca? Say why.

stretch.question: Explain two different beliefs about God in Britain.

debate.statement: There is no good reason to believe in God today.
agree: Atheists like Sophia say there is no evidence for God, and evidence is what proof needs.
Science can explain how the world works without needing a God to have made it.
disagree: Theists like Amir say God listens when they pray, which is a reason from experience.
Agnostics like Luca say nobody can be certain, so nobody can rule God out either.
debate.how_to_win: Name the three views, use one example of each, then give your own view with a reason.

quickfire.q: Define theism.
Define atheist.
Describe what happens in Christian prayer.
What day is the Jummah prayer?
Give the difference between an atheist and theist.
Why might someone be an agnostic?

lessons.title: Religious artefacts
lessons.big_question: What are religious artefacts? Why are they important?
aims: DESCRIBE — what a religious artefact is
DISCUSS — why certain objects matter to believers
EXPLAIN — two artefacts from two different religions

questions: Is there an object that is important to you? Which one and why?
Define agnostic in a full sentence.
Name one thing Muslims use to help them pray.

learn.caption: Artefacts in Christianity and Islam
rows: Prayer mat: a clean place to pray
Compass: finds the way to Mecca

source.quote: A religious artefact is an object that can have religious, cultural or personal significance. All religious traditions have objects that are used in worship or in festivals.
source.attrib: — Unit 1 lesson slides, on religious artefacts
source.task: Draw one Christian artefact and one Muslim artefact. Label each with what it is used for.

stretch.question: Explain two religious artefacts from two different religions.

debate.statement: Religious objects are just ordinary things with no real power.
agree: A prayer mat is only cloth and a rosary is only beads, so the object itself does nothing.
Believers could still pray perfectly well without owning any of these objects at all.
disagree: A crucifix reminds Christians of God's forgiveness, so the object carries a huge meaning.
A prayer mat gives Muslims a clean place to pray anywhere, so it really does help worship.
debate.how_to_win: Say what the object does for the believer, not what it is made of, then judge.

quickfire.q: Define theist.
Why might someone be an agnostic?
Name the three views people hold about God.
What is a fact? Give an example.
What is a religious artefact?

lessons.title: Religious symbols
lessons.big_question: Why are religious symbols important to believers?
aims: DESCRIBE — the main symbol of five world religions
DISCUSS — the difference between a sign and a symbol
EXPLAIN — what two religious symbols mean to believers

questions: Why do you think religious symbols exist?
Why are religious symbols important?
Name two religious artefacts you learned last lesson.

learn.caption: The main symbols of five religions
rows: Hinduism: Aum, the most holy sound

source.quote: Some ideas and feelings are very complicated and cannot be explained in words. One way to do it is through the use of symbols. Symbols express complex ideas in a simple way.
source.attrib: — Unit 1 lesson slides, on religious symbols
source.task: Draw the cross and the Aum symbol. Beside each, write one sentence about what it means.

stretch.question: Explain two religious symbols from two different religions.

debate.statement: A symbol can say more than words ever could.
agree: The slides say some feelings are too complicated for words, so symbols express them simply.
One glance at a crucifix reminds a Christian of the whole story of Jesus dying on the cross.
disagree: A symbol only works if you already know its meaning, so words have to explain it first.
The crescent moon was used by the city of Byzantium before Islam, so meanings can change.
debate.how_to_win: Give one symbol whose meaning is obvious and one that must be taught, then decide.

lessons.title: Summative assessment
lessons.big_question: How much have I learned about beliefs this unit?
aims: DESCRIBE — the key words from the whole Beliefs unit
DISCUSS — which topics I still need to revise
EXPLAIN — two views about God and two forms of prayer

questions: Define belief, fact and opinion in three full sentences.
Name the three views people hold about God.
Name two religious artefacts and say who uses them.

learn.caption: Topics your summative test covers
rows: Two reasons why we study RE

source.quote: Theism is the belief there is God. Atheism is the belief there is no god. Agnosticism is doubt if there is or is not a god.
source.attrib: — Unit 1 summative test, key word definitions
source.task: Learn these three definitions by heart. Then cover them and write each one from memory.

stretch.question: Explain two views about God and two forms of prayer.

debate.statement: An end of unit test is the best way to show what you know.
agree: A test makes you revise everything, so you find the gaps you did not know you had.
Comparing it with the baseline test proves exactly how much progress you have made.
disagree: Some people panic in tests, so the mark can show their nerves and not their knowledge.
RE is about discussing beliefs, and a written test cannot capture a good discussion.
debate.how_to_win: Say what a test can and cannot measure, then give a clear judgement with one reason.
